conventions.bit_numbering: Manual MSB-first names are preserved: bit 0 is the most-significant bit.
conventions.active_level: low means the printed manual shows an overbar; encoded and data signals have no Boolean asserted level.
conventions.clock: Unless a signal says asynchronous, logical bus events are observed at SYSCLK bus-clock boundaries. Electrical setup/hold is outside this source set.
conventions.oe: oe_class names a shared output-enable rule below; input-only signals use none.
conventions.verification: Overbars and directions were checked on rendered Figure 7-1 and the rendered signal-description headings. Timing text was checked against Chapter 7 prose.

oe_classes.none: Input or supply; the processor does not drive it.
oe_classes.dedicated: Dedicated push-pull output in normal operation; reset/checkstop can release processor outputs as stated for HRESET and CKSTP_IN.
oe_classes.address_tenure: Driven with the processor-owned address tenure and released to high impedance one bus clock after AACK unless the signal-specific rule says earlier.
oe_classes.address_busy: ABB is asserted after a qualified BG, negated at least one-half bus clock after AACK, then released.
oe_classes.transfer_start: TS is driven for one bus clock with address/attributes and is released when ABB is negated.
oe_classes.address_retry_shared: Shared response: drive asserted when retrying a snoop; on release use the manual's half-processor-cycle high-Z, one-bus-cycle driven-negated, then high-Z sequence unless precharge is disabled.
oe_classes.data_busy: DBB is asserted after a qualified DBG, negated at least one-half bus clock after the final/only TA, then released. On a read, DRTRY can continue data-bus exclusion after DBB is negated.
oe_classes.write_data: Driven only for processor write beats while the processor owns DBB; released on the bus clock after the final/only TA.
oe_classes.open_drain: Open-drain output; an external pull-up supplies negation and the processor otherwise releases the pin.
oe_classes.clock_out: CLK_OUT is high impedance by default and driven only under HID0 clock-output selections; PID7v also drives it at processor frequency while HRESET is asserted.
oe_classes.jtag_output: Driven by the JTAG TAP when applicable.
oe_classes.test_unspecified: Direction is visible in Figure 7-1, but normal drive rules are outside the user's manual.

signals.name: BR
signals.qualification: Requests address-bus ownership; may cancel; negation is at least one bus clock after an accepted qualified grant and for at least one clock after ARTRY.
signals.reset_mode: Released with other outputs after HRESET/CKSTP_IN rules.

signals.name: BG
signals.qualification: Qualified only while BG is asserted and ABB and the ARTRY result following AACK are negated; not accepted between TS and AACK.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: ABB
signals.qualification: As input, asserted means another master owns the address bus and blocks a qualified grant.
signals.reset_mode: Released with bidirectional outputs under reset/checkstop.

signals.name: TS
signals.qualification: Processor output coincides with ABB and valid address/attributes for one cycle; as input it marks the single snoop sampling cycle and need not coincide with external ABB assertion.
signals.reset_mode: Released with bidirectional outputs under reset/checkstop.

signals.name: A[0:31]
signals.qualification: Output physical address is valid with TS and held through AACK; input address is sampled only in the TS cycle for snooping.
signals.reset_mode: Input receiver is not disabled by reduced-pinout mode.

signals.name: AP[0:3]
signals.qualification: Odd parity for A byte groups 0:7, 8:15, 16:23, and 24:31; input follows address snoop timing and parity checking is HID0-controlled.
signals.reset_mode: HID0[EICE] remaps AP to pipeline-tracking outputs; reduced-pinout disables receivers and drives low when normally driven.

signals.name: APE
signals.qualification: With HID0[EBA] enabled, asserts on the second bus cycle after a snooped TS when address parity is wrong; released on the third.
signals.reset_mode: Disabled and always high-Z in reduced-pinout mode.

signals.name: TT[0:4]
signals.qualification: Transfer command encoding; output follows address timing. Figure 7-1 and the section introduction call all five bits input/output and Table 7-2 consumes TT4, but the input subsection says TT[0:3]; this editorial inconsistency remains flagged. Snoop meanings are Table 7-2; PID7v HID0[ABE] address-only overrides are Table 7-3.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: TBST
signals.qualification: Asserted denotes a cache-line burst. In 32-bit mode an uncached 8-byte two-beat transfer still leaves TBST negated.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: TSIZ[0:2]
signals.qualification: Together with TBST encodes transfer size; Tables 7-5/7-6 and 8-4/8-5 define legal aligned and misaligned combinations.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: GBL
signals.qualification: Processor output marks a global transaction; asserted input qualifies snoop participation and parity checking.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: CI
signals.qualification: Asserted marks caching-inhibited access.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: WT
signals.qualification: Asserted marks write-through access.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: CSE[0:1]
signals.qualification: Cache-set element encoding; Table 8-9 maps 00/01/10/11 to sets 0/1/2/3.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: TC[0:1]
signals.qualification: Transfer-code encoding for privilege and instruction/data character; definition is in Section 7.2.4.4.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: AACK
signals.qualification: One-cycle address termination pulse. Earliest is the cycle after TS, except generic 1:1/1.5:1 modes require one wait; qualified ARTRY is sampled in the following cycle.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: ARTRY
signals.qualification: Early ARTRY can begin during address tenure; qualified ARTRY is asserted in the cycle after AACK. Either retries the entire transaction and aborts an associated data tenure.
signals.reset_mode: Late cancellation after TA is forbidden in no-DRTRY mode; released with outputs under reset/checkstop.

signals.name: SYSCLK
signals.qualification: Bus-interface clock and PLL reference; must not stop or vary during normal operation.
signals.reset_mode: Generic Chapter 7 lists 1:1 through 4:1; PID7v-specific Chapter 1 permits 2:1 through 6:1 and excludes 1:1/1.5:1.

signals.name: CLK_OUT
signals.qualification: Test/monitor clock selected by HID0[SBCLK,ECLK]; HID0[EICE] also enables processor-clock tracking output.
signals.reset_mode: PID7v drives processor frequency while HRESET is asserted, then returns to default high-Z when HRESET is negated.

signals.name: PLL_CFG[0:3]
signals.qualification: PLL ratio/configuration strap; must remain stable during normal operation and change only under HRESET or sleep.
signals.reset_mode: Chosen PID7v ratio must follow PID7v-specific Chapter 1 limits plus the missing hardware specification.

signals.name: DBG
signals.qualification: Qualified only while DBG is asserted and DBB, DRTRY, and the ARTRY result associated with the address tenure are negated.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: DBWO
signals.qualification: Sampled only with a qualified DBG. Selects the next queued write ahead of an older read; if no write is queued, the next read proceeds.
signals.reset_mode: Keep negated unless the system intentionally implements enveloped writes.

signals.name: DBB
signals.qualification: As input, asserted means another master owns the data bus and blocks a qualified grant. On a read, DRTRY can keep other masters from asserting DBB after the prior master's DBB has negated.
signals.reset_mode: Released with bidirectional outputs under reset/checkstop.

signals.name: DH[0:31]
signals.qualification: High four byte lanes. Processor drives writes and samples reads with TA; burst beat advances after each accepted TA.
signals.reset_mode: Only data lanes used in 32-bit and reduced-pinout modes.

signals.name: DL[0:31]
signals.qualification: Low four byte lanes. Processor drives writes and samples reads with TA in 64-bit mode.
signals.reset_mode: In 32-bit mode inputs are ignored and write values are low; reduced-pinout also disables input receivers and drives low when normally driven.

signals.name: DP[0:7]
signals.qualification: Odd parity per data byte; input parity checks all enabled lanes independent of transfer size and are HID0-controlled.
signals.reset_mode: HID0[EICE] remaps DP to tracking outputs. DP4:7 unused in 32-bit mode; all DP disabled in reduced-pinout mode.

signals.name: DPE
signals.qualification: With data-parity checking enabled, asserts on the second cycle after TA unless that beat is cancelled by DRTRY; released on the third.
signals.reset_mode: Disabled and always high-Z in reduced-pinout mode.

signals.name: DBDIS
signals.qualification: Write-only control. Assertion makes processor data/parity high-Z in the following cycle while DBB ownership and termination monitoring continue.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: TA
signals.qualification: Acknowledges one data beat; one assertion is required per beat. It precedes any DRTRY assertion and can be withheld to insert data wait cycles.
signals.reset_mode: Should not precede AACK where the system depends on ARTRY cancellation.

signals.name: DRTRY
signals.qualification: Read-only late cancellation, asserted on the cycle after TA; may remain asserted for several cycles. Negation confirms the previously acknowledged read beat.
signals.reset_mode: Sampled when HRESET is negated: asserted selects no-DRTRY mode; negated selects normal mode. Must never assert later in no-DRTRY mode.

signals.name: TEA
signals.qualification: One-cycle error termination. Section 7.2.8.3 permits it while DBB is asserted or the cycle after TA on a read; Section 8.4.4.2 explicitly also permits it while DRTRY is asserted on a read, including an extended retry after DBB negates. TA and DRTRY are ignored; DBB is released in the next cycle if still asserted.
signals.reset_mode: Can cause machine check/checkstop according to MSR state; data already admitted to a GPR/cache is not invalidated.

signals.name: INT
signals.qualification: Asynchronous level-sensitive external interrupt; hold asserted until taken.
signals.reset_mode: Serviced when MSR[EE] permits.

signals.name: SMI
signals.qualification: Asynchronous level-sensitive system-management interrupt; hold asserted until taken.
signals.reset_mode: Serviced when MSR[EE] permits.

signals.name: MCP
signals.qualification: Asynchronous negative-edge-sensitive machine check; hold asserted at least two bus clocks.
signals.reset_mode: Meaning depends on HID0[EMCP] and MSR[ME]; can force checkstop and release outputs.

signals.name: CKSTP_IN
signals.qualification: Asynchronous nonmaskable checkstop; once asserted remains asserted until reset.
signals.reset_mode: Gates internal clocks and releases all outputs except CKSTP_OUT.

signals.name: CKSTP_OUT
signals.qualification: Asynchronous indication that the processor stopped.
signals.reset_mode: Negated by HRESET; remains the one output not released by CKSTP_IN.

signals.name: HRESET
signals.qualification: Asynchronous hard reset; output drivers become high-Z within five clocks. Hold at least 255 clocks after PLL lock; electrical timing requires the missing hardware specification.
signals.reset_mode: Negation triggers hard-reset completion and samples DRTRY, TLBISYNC, and QACK mode straps.

signals.name: SRESET
signals.qualification: Asynchronous negative-edge-sensitive soft reset; may be negated after two bus cycles.
signals.reset_mode: Warm reset behavior; has extra test-mode functionality.

signals.name: RSRV
signals.qualification: Synchronous representation of the reservation coherency bit used by lwarx/stwcx.
signals.reset_mode: Disabled in reduced-pinout mode and driven low when it would normally be driven.

signals.name: QREQ
signals.qualification: May change on any cycle and remains asserted through quiescence; requests snooped activity terminate or pause.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: QACK
signals.qualification: After QREQ, may assert on any cycle and must remain asserted at least one bus clock.
signals.reset_mode: Sampled when HRESET is negated: asserted selects full pinout; negated selects reduced pinout.

signals.name: TBEN
signals.qualification: May change on any cycle; asserted enables time-base counting and negated stops it.
signals.reset_mode: No startup strap role stated.

signals.name: TLBISYNC
signals.qualification: May change on any cycle; asserted stalls instruction execution after tlbsync until negated.
signals.reset_mode: Sampled when HRESET is negated: asserted selects 32-bit data bus; negated selects 64-bit.

signals.name: TDI
signals.qualification: Serial scan input; scan data is latched on rising TCK.
signals.reset_mode: TAP use only.

signals.name: TDO
signals.qualification: Serial scan output; no weak pull-up is provided.
signals.reset_mode: TAP use only.

signals.name: TMS
signals.qualification: TAP controller mode input; sampled with rising TCK.
signals.reset_mode: TAP use only.

signals.name: TCK
signals.qualification: JTAG scan clock; scan input is latched on its rising edge.
signals.reset_mode: TAP use only.

signals.name: TRST
signals.qualification: Asynchronous TAP reset; may assert with HRESET.
signals.reset_mode: Keeps JTAG from interfering with normal operation.

signals.name: TEST[0:2]
signals.qualification: Figure 7-1 identifies three LSSD test-control pins; detailed operation is explicitly outside this user's manual.
signals.reset_mode: Tie/state requirements require the applicable hardware specification.

signals.name: VDD
signals.qualification: Core supply; no electrical distinction from OVDD is stated for 603e.
signals.reset_mode: Electrical values require the hardware specification.

signals.name: OVDD
signals.qualification: I/O-named supply; no electrical distinction from VDD is stated for 603e.
signals.reset_mode: Electrical values require the hardware specification.

signals.name: AVDD
signals.qualification: PLL supply.
signals.reset_mode: Connection/filter requirements require the hardware specification.

signals.name: GND
signals.qualification: Ground; no electrical distinction from OGND is stated for 603e.
signals.reset_mode: Electrical values require the hardware specification.

signals.name: OGND
signals.qualification: I/O-named ground; no electrical distinction from GND is stated for 603e.
signals.reset_mode: Electrical values require the hardware specification.
